feedback.problem: If ${z}_{1}=1-12\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=8\text{i}$, then ${z}_{1}$ divided by ${z}_{2}$ equals
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we set up the fraction:

$$
\frac{1-12\text{i}}{8\text{i}}
$$

The denominator is the imaginary number $8\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+8\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-8\text{i},$ or simply $-8\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-8\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}} & =\frac{1-12\text{i}}{8\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{1-12\text{i}}{8\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-8\text{i}}{-8\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-8\text{i}+96{\text{i}}^{2}}{-64{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-8\text{i}+96(-1)}{-64(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-96-8\text{i}}{64}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-96-8\text{i}}{64}=-\frac{96}{64}-\frac{8}{64}\text{i}=-\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{8}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
